chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the day in which there is doubt, and it is not known whether it is from the month of Ramadan or from Sha'ban, so he said: 'The month of Ramadan is a month among the months, which is affected by what affects the months in terms of increase and decrease, so fast by the sighting [of the moon] and break your fast by the sighting [of the moon], and I do not like for anyone to precede it by fasting a day,' and he mentioned the hadith.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting when there is doubt about the start of Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of 'sighting-based' determination for Ramadan's onset, emphasizing that the month's variable length (29 or 30 days) requires waiting for visual confirmation rather than relying solely on calculation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential preference for actual sighting (ru'yah) over astronomical calculation (hisab) for the start of the month, while strictly prohibiting the premature fasting of a specific 'day of doubt' (yawm al-shakk) as a distinct act of worship. The hadith reinforces the practical application of the Quranic command to fast Ramadan, linking the physical act of fasting directly to the observable lunar cycle.
